institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: there were not that many places you could choose from. I wanted to stay in Europe but still get to experience something that differs from Denmark. And also where it was possible to get some courses that sounded interesting and relevant for my study in english

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was in general quite a lot of information and things you needed to do so it was nice that everyone had to do it so you could help each other out. A lot of things here are very old school where you have to show up in person and do actual paper work

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: there was an info session with what needed to be done

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult i only got offered the one dorm I ended up staying at even though i applied for multiple and tried to apply early as well

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: i wanted to live at a dorm because of the social aspect we are used to in Denmark. But that was not the case at the dorm i stayed at and i feel like that is what i heard from a lot of other people. If you want something more social i think you should rent a room in an apartment with other young people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there has been a lot of back an forth and especially problems with documentation from my home university which has blurred my experience a lot. but i think in general they have been very quick at responding and helping.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is a lot where you have to show up in person and you can not register for courses before you have been there physically so you have to be there early to get the courses you want

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The contact person was very nice, helpful and  responded very quickly

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up being quite successful but was waitlisted for a lot and also for one course for a very long time, so i had to register for to many courses because i did not know if i would get off the waitlist

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is all gonna be solved, don't stress to much, and try to get here before semester start so you can register for courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the master courses were easier than the bachelor course( i only took 2 BA courses), also regarding the exams. but the level is generally lower than UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses are smaller classes and there is a lot of different types of classes and excursions

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: German Intensive Course before the start of the semester, Field trip viticulture and oenology, Gender, nutrition and right to food, Food structure, Food packaging technology, German for Science (BOKU specific topics), Automatic identification technology in food industry, Intercultural competence - Changing perspectives in a diverse (working) environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think doing som german classes is nice (there are all levels) it was a nice way to meet other exchange students and was there i met a lot of the people i ended up spending time with. The wine trip was also very nive and food packaging. i also heard good things about World wines and viticulture so I am a bit sad i did not have that

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I think the food in supermarkets was more expensive than I expected (a bit more expensive than Denmark) also if you want to join a fitness it is very expensive (100€ pr month)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out, living (i had a high rent  compared to other students)  also

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined 3 sport activities through the university (USI) this was very nice and cheap. there were also a lot of social events for ERASMUS students (trips, hikes, parties etc)

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: befriend vienna has a lot of nice social things, going to a lot of museums and traveling around austria and the boardering countries. Also if in the summer semester go to Albert & tina it is outdoor party at a museum in the evening

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: i went on a trip to Croatia and Slovenia and then also a trip around austria both i would recommend

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: i think it was quite easy the locals are very friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: they keep much to them self but maybe going to USI sport

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: nothing comes to mind

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the architecture, and the restaurants, cafes and especially in the late spring/ summer there are very many activities around the city (outdoor movies, outdoor parties, dancing classes etc)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
The process of making a schedule is very time consuming and annoying but use a lot of time on it, that really pays of 
I would recommend living in district 1 or 4-9 if possible, it is a bit more expensive but i think it is worth it 
It is very centrally placed so you can get to experience so much of Europe very easily and there is both nice cities and nature close by

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I think taking german classes was very nice (even though I hated german in high school) 
it is nice to be able to speak and understand a bit of german when living here

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting out of my comfort zone and meeting so many people from different cultures

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: having to built a social network from the ground and trying not to be stressed about all the administrative work

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: go on exchange it is the best experience !

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
